para.dtcname: Belt Clamping Pressure Sensor Circuit (Function Check)

content5.ptxt: The engine control computer performs learning control of the belt clamping force based on the belt clamping pressure signal detected by the oil pressure sensor.
P0841/C8 and P2829/77 are function diagnoses detected when the hydraulic pressure sensor output value is high even though the hydraulic pressure command value is low.
If DTCs for other belt clamping pressure sensor circuits are output at the same time, it is necessary to troubleshoot starting from the DTCs other than P0841/C8 and P2829/77.

item.ptxt: Be sure to perform this after inspecting and adjusting the engine.
Perform with the CVT at normal operating temperature (50-100°C).
Perform the test with the A/C OFF.
Do not continuously run the test for 5 seconds or more.
Perform the test in a place with a high μ (coefficient of friction), such as on asphalt, so that the tires do not spin.

test1.ptxt: Apply the parking brake and chock the wheels.
Connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3 and turn the power ON.
Following SST (TaSCAN), select [Active Test] -> [TC Terminal ON], and display [ECU Data Monitor] -> [AT Hydraulic Pressure] and [Engine Speed].
Perform the Active Test (TC terminal ON condition), depress the brake pedal firmly with the left foot, and inspect the hydraulic pressure at idle speed (N position) and at stall speed (D position).

testgrp.testtitle: TaSCAN (A/T / CVT Learned Value Initialization, G Sensor 0-point Learning and CVT Hydraulic Pressure Learning)

item.ptxt: Initializing the learned values clears both the G sensor 0 point learning and CVT hydraulic pressure learning values, so when replacing the parts in the table below, be sure to perform both G sensor 0 point learning and CVT hydraulic pressure learning after performing AT/CVT learned value initialization.
Continuously Variable Transaxle
Engine Control Computer
Oil Pressure Sensor
Yaw Rate Sensor
After performing AT/CVT learned value initialization, be sure to perform G sensor 0-point learning first, and then CVT hydraulic pressure learning.
Be sure to place the vehicle on a level surface and perform 0 point learning.
Do not subject the vehicle to vibration while 0 point learning is in progress.
